new.title: Drink a local draught at Dornröschen, Hanover's oldest beer garden
new.desc: Biergarten Dornröschen sits on the Leine bank in the Nordstadt and dates to 1875, making it the oldest beer garden in Hanover. It pours several local draught beers and also serves coffee and cake.
new.tip: Go on a dry summer afternoon and bring a bike, as the Leine path runs past the garden.
new.q: Dornröschen Biergarten, In den Kämpen 54, Nordstadt, Hannover

new.title: Sit under old trees at the See Biergarten on the Maschsee
new.desc: The See Biergarten stands directly on the Maschsee shore at Arthur-Menge-Ufer, close to the Neues Rathaus. It serves Flammkuchen, grill dishes and cold draught beer under old trees.
new.tip: Arrive before sunset for a lakeside table; combine it with a walk along the north shore.

new.title: Order the house curry sausage at anna leine
new.desc: A small café and kitchen at Am Hohen Ufer with a view of the Leine and the Nanas. Its recommended dish is the anna leine special curry sausage with home-made curry sauce, and it also offers soups, salads, cakes and vegan dishes.
new.tip: Open weekdays from 8:00, Saturday 10:00 to 15:00 and closed on Sunday; lunch menu from 11:00.
new.q: anna leine, Am Hohen Ufer 3, Hannover

new.title: Taste coffee roasted on site at 24grad
new.desc: 24grad is a café and coffee roastery at Engelbosteler Damm in the Nordstadt, opened on 24 December 2009. The coffee is roasted in-house in a nostalgically furnished space.
new.tip: Buy a bag of beans to take home; the roastery is a short ride from Königsworther Platz.
new.q: 24grad Café und Kaffeerösterei, Engelbosteler Damm 52, Hannover

new.title: Eat a vegan Thai dish at Hippo Organic Vegan
new.desc: Hippo is an organic vegan café and restaurant on Marienstraße near the main station. It serves an extensive vegan breakfast and vegan Thai cuisine.
new.tip: Good for brunch or a quick dinner before a train; check the menu online for daily specials.

new.title: Have lunch at Cafve in the Hafven creative hub
new.desc: Cafve is the café of the Hafven creative centre, which also hosts co-working spaces and workshops. It serves salads, wraps, breakfast bowls and home-baked cakes made partly from regional organic produce, with coffee from local roasters.
new.tip: All-day breakfast on Saturdays and Sundays until 15:00; the Friday community breakfast runs 9:30 to 11:00.

new.title: Eat schnitzel or Currywurst at Alexander in the Altstadt
new.desc: Alexander is a casual restaurant in vintage décor on Prinzenstraße, serving schnitzel, Currywurst and regional dishes. It sits a few steps from the opera house.
new.tip: Order the Currywurst, Hanover's classic fast-food dish, and expect a relaxed pub-like crowd.

new.title: Eat Currywurst on Linden's market square at Centrum
new.desc: Centrum is a bar and restaurant at the Lindener Marktplatz, serving burgers and a classic Currywurst, with a vegan version also on the menu. It is a meeting point in Linden-Mitte.
new.tip: Sit outside on the square in summer; the vegan Currywurst is a good test for sceptics.

new.title: Try Bohemian dishes at Schwejk in Celle
new.desc: Schwejk is a Czech-German restaurant on Kanzleistraße in Celle's Altstadt, listed in Schlemmer Atlas under Bohemian and German cuisine. Reviewers praise the authentic Bohemian food, and the menu includes toasted Topinky bread.
new.tip: Open evenings only on most days; book ahead because locals fill it.

new.title: Have a Brotzeit at Thaers Wirtshaus in Celle
new.desc: Thaers Wirtshaus is a regional inn on Thaerplatz in Celle that serves German dishes and Brotzeit plates such as Münchner Wurstsalat and cheese Stulle. It is listed on hannover.de among local German restaurants.
new.tip: Reviews note slightly higher prices than average; the kitchen is open until about 22:00.

new.title: Eat a giant pancake at Pfannekuchen in Hameln
new.desc: Restaurant Pfannekuchen on Hummenstraße occupies a centuries-old townhouse and serves more than 40 sweet and savoury pancake variations. A gluten-free selection is also offered.
new.tip: Open daily from about 11:00 to 21:30; go early on weekends.

new.title: Dine at the Rattenkrug, an inn since 1870 in Hameln
new.desc: The Rattenkrug on Bäckerstraße has been used as a Gaststätte since 1870 and has carried that name since. It serves Bavarian, regional and German dishes in the Altstadt.
new.tip: Wanderlog shows about 4.3 stars from over 1,300 reviews; outdoor tables are open in good weather.

new.title: Dine in the Knochenhauer-Amtshaus at KA7
new.desc: KA7 is the restaurant and café inside the Knochenhauer-Amtshaus on Hildesheim's Marktplatz, serving German and vegan dishes and a selection of Einbecker beers. The timber-framed guild house is the best-known building on the square.
new.tip: Book a table with a view of the market square; open for lunch and dinner.
new.q: KA7 Restaurant im Knochenhauer-Amtshaus, Markt 7, Hildesheim

new.title: Eat Buchweizentorte at Café Höpen Idyll in Schneverdingen
new.desc: Café-Pension Höpen Idyll serves only home-made cakes and tortes, with the Lüneburg Heath buckwheat torte as its signature. About 14 varieties are available daily including gluten-free ones, with a view of up to 60 km.
new.tip: Visit after a heath walk; waffles with cream and cherries are served in winter.

new.title: Drink craft beer at Das Freie in Rethmar
new.desc: Gutshofbrauerei Das Freie is a craft brewery on the historic Gutshof Rethmar estate in Sehnde, with a beer garden. The restored country estate is popular for day trips from Hanover.
new.tip: Combine with a walk on the estate; check opening times by phone before visiting.
new.q: Gutshofbrauerei Das Freie, Gutsstraße 16, Rethmar, Sehnde

new.title: Swim at the Strandbad Maschsee lido
new.desc: The Strandbad is a beach and lido on the southeast shore of the Maschsee, popular for swimming and sunbathing. It is a short walk from the Döhrener Turm tram stop (lines 1, 2, 8).
new.tip: Go in the bathing season; bring sandals as the lake bottom is soft.

new.title: Climb at Kletterbar, Lower Saxony's largest climbing hall
new.desc: Kletterbar in the Brink-Hafen district has more than 3,300 m² of climbing and bouldering area with walls up to 16 m and a 700 m² covered outdoor zone. It has auto-belays for solo climbers and a bistro with pizza.
new.tip: Gear rental is available; first-timers must register on site and beginners can use the bouldering area.

new.title: See a gig at the Capitol in Linden
new.desc: The Capitol is a concert and party club on the Schwarzer Bär square in Linden-Mitte, in the former Capitol-Lichtspiele cinema. It hosts touring acts and club nights.
new.tip: Check the programme online; tram lines 9 and 17 stop at Schwarzer Bär.

new.title: Catch a concert at Kulturzentrum Faust
new.desc: Kulturzentrum Faust occupies a former factory site in Linden-Nord and runs several halls, including the Mephisto and the 60er Jahre Halle, for concerts and parties. The wider Faust-Gelände is a reused industrial area.
new.tip: Events are listed on kulturzentrum-faust.de; the beer garden on site is open in summer.

new.title: Tour the Gilde Brauerei, Hanover's oldest brewery
new.desc: The Gilde Brauerei traces its origins to 1546 and uses the Broyhan-Taler as its emblem. It has stood on Hildesheimer Straße since 1870, with the modern plant built from 1970 to 1977, and offers a brewery tour behind the scenes.
new.tip: Book the tour in advance and check gilde-brauerei.com for dates.

new.title: Boulder at urban apes in Döhren-Wülfel
new.desc: urban apes is a climbing and bouldering hall on Am Mittelfelde in Döhren-Wülfel, one of three bouldering venues listed for Hanover on Urban Sports Club.
new.tip: Check hours and day-pass prices on the hall's own site.
new.q: urban apes Hannover, Am Mittelfelde 39, Hannover

new.title: Cruise the Aller on the Wappen von Celle
new.desc: The passenger ship Wappen von Celle runs scheduled trips on the Aller from Celle. Regular sailings run from early May to the end of September.
new.tip: Check the timetable on celle.travel; sailings are seasonal.

new.title: Paddle the Aller by canoe with Meyer's Kanatour
new.desc: Meyer's Kanatour runs canoe tours on the Aller and Örtze departing near Celle city centre, for 2 to 200 people. Extras include archery and axe throwing.
new.tip: Tours start from about 20 euros per person; book by phone.

new.title: Take a Weser boat from Hameln with Flotte Weser
new.desc: Flotte Weser operates excursion boats on the Weser and has a landing stage in Hameln. Its fleet runs on a fixed summer timetable, with charters available all year.
new.tip: Check flotte-weser.de for the timetable, as low water can suspend service.

new.title: Visit Kloster Loccum, a living Cistercian monastery
new.desc: Kloster Loccum near Rehburg-Loccum is, with Maulbronn, the best-preserved Cistercian complex in Germany. Public guided tours of about an hour run on weekends from April to October at 15:00.
new.tip: Tours leave from in front of the collegiate church; check the monastery website as events can cancel them.

new.title: Admire St. Godehard, Hildesheim's Romanesque basilica
new.desc: Construction of St. Godehard and its monastery began in 1133, the year Godehard was canonized, and Bishop Adelog consecrated the church in 1172. It is a Romanesque basilica with a double choir and has held the title Basilica minor since 1963.
new.tip: Open to visitors outside services; combine with the cathedral and St. Michael's.

new.title: See light art at the Kunstmuseum Celle
new.desc: The Kunstmuseum Celle calls itself the world's first 24-hour art museum. Its glass cube glows in colour from inside at night, and light-art installations can be seen from outside after closing.
new.tip: Come after dark to see the cube lit; it stands next to Celle Castle.
